full_translation_en:
National Parliament
National Assembly
Twenty-first Session
Complete Record of Proceedings
May 19, 2083
Wednesday
Meeting Number - 13
The National Assembly's meeting today commenced at 1:18 PM under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Chairperson Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
Honourable Chairperson:- The proceedings of the National Assembly's meeting today (1:18 PM) commence. The proceedings can also be adjourned. If there is applause, it can be adjourned. Honourable members, what was it? It is understood that time was sought through applause. I will call the honourable members one by one. Other honourable members, please remain seated and listen. First, Honourable Member Padam Bahadur Pariyar, time 7 minutes.
Honourable Mr. Padam Bahadur Pariyar (Nepali Congress):- Honourable Chairperson, regarding the extremely sensitive issue of border problems connected with territorial integrity and national security, the irresponsible statement made by the Honourable Prime Minister Balendra Shah on May 17th, standing at the rostrum of the respected House of Representatives, that 'we have also encroached on India's land in many places,' has drawn our attention. Our party, the Nepali Congress, issued a statement on May 17th and clarified our party's position on this matter. Specifically, this statement made by the head of government in a dignified forum like the parliament, without any historical facts or evidence, in a casual manner, which is against national interest, is unforgivable, objectionable, and highly condemnable. Honourable Chairperson, this fully exposes the intention and weak political and diplomatic understanding of the head of government towards national pride. Not only that, the Nepali Congress party does not accept the aimless statements made by the head of government regarding border issues. Honourable Chairperson, we are all aware that approximately 372 square kilometers of Nepali territory, including Limpiyadhura, Lipulek, and Kalapani, have been encroached upon. However, we cannot accept this admission by the head of government, made with malicious and unnecessary intent, that Nepal has also encroached upon and encroached upon India's land. Honourable Chairperson, what is even more ridiculous and sensitive is the claim made by the head of government that talks are ongoing with Britain regarding border issues. This is extremely objectionable and ridiculous.
Honourable Chairperson, it is necessary to clarify whether this is the official stance of the government or the official stance of the Rastriya Swatantra Party. Not only that, Honourable Chairperson, yesterday, the chairman of the ruling party, Rastriya Swatantra Party, published an article in an Indian newspaper today, interpreting the mutual relationship between Nepal and India in such a casual manner that he views Nepal's historical, strategic, and multidimensional relationship through a simple development model, as a development partner model. We are also seriously concerned about this extremely narrow perspective presented by the Honourable Chairperson. Specifically, the statement made by the Prime Minister, which is contrary to diplomatic decorum, is not only condemnable in itself, but also, the chairman of the same party has also stifled Nepal's historical relationship with India and stifled its multidimensional relationship by framing it solely within a development model. This is ignorance of knowledge.
There are many types of fraud in Nepal. Various types of fraud occur. Recently, the issue of cooperative fraud became prominent. I feel this is also a kind of fraud. Therefore, such frauds based on ignorance against Nepalis are unacceptable. Absolutely unacceptable. Therefore, from our party, we want to clearly state in this House that either the Honourable Prime Minister should come to the House and state in which place, how many square kilometers or how many square meters or inches of Nepali land or Indian land has been encroached upon by Nepalis? Let's clarify it in the House with facts and evidence.
Or the Honourable Prime Minister should come to the House and say, 'I spoke outside of facts, I spoke in haste, I spoke emotionally, I am sorry.' The Prime Minister's home is the parliament. The Prime Minister's place is the parliament. The Honourable Prime Minister should have the courage to come to the parliament and say without shame, without hesitation, 'I spoke outside of facts, I spoke in haste, I spoke emotionally, I am sorry.' If he cannot do even that, then Honourable Chairperson, on behalf of the Nepali Congress and other opposition parties, this dignified House has been subjected to such a light attack, a serious attack, forgive me, a serious attack on Nepal's sovereignty and territorial integrity by the Honourable Prime Minister, and an act contrary to Nepal's diplomatic decorum. This cannot be forgotten, and the Nepali Congress is not ready to proceed with the proceedings of this House. The Nepali Congress and all other parties are not ready to proceed with the business of the House. I wish to inform you of this. Thank you.
Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Ghanashyam Rizal, time 7 minutes.
Honourable Mr. Ghanashyam Rizal (Communist Party of Nepal):
Honourable Chairperson, I express my serious disagreement and concern regarding the statement made by the Honourable Prime Minister Balendra Shah on May 17, 2083, during the meeting of the House of Representatives, that not only India has encroached on Nepal's land, but Nepal has also encroached on India's land in many places, which is against Nepal's territorial integrity and national interest. This is our party's stance. Even when India has not accused Nepal of encroaching on its land, and without any facts or evidence, the Nepal-India Joint Border Commission has publicly completed the demarcation work for 98 percent of the land, excluding some disputed areas like Kalapani, Lipulek, and Limpiyadhura, and the Government of Nepal has also issued its updated map of its territory. In this situation, the Honourable Prime Minister Balendra Shah, who is a senior leader of the ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party, made such a statement on the eve of his visit to India. On what basis and with what intention was such a statement made? I heartily request the Honourable Prime Minister, through the Honourable Chairperson, to inform this House and correct his mistake by apologizing to the Nepali people through this House.
Matters related to the nation's sovereignty, territorial integrity, and borders are extremely sensitive and of national importance. It is necessary to speak on such matters only after gathering national consensus based on facts and evidence. Honourable Chairperson, the statement made by the Honourable Prime Minister Balendra Shah, whether knowingly or unknowingly, from the parliament's rostrum, has already begun to cause problems in some border areas with India, as reported in various media outlets. Therefore, it is our party's stance that this meeting cannot proceed until the Honourable Prime Minister corrects his mistake and apologizes to the nation through the parliament. I convey this through the Honourable Chairperson to this House and conclude my remarks. Thank you.
Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Roshni Mechhe, time seven minutes.
Honourable Mr. Roshni Mechhe (Nepal Communist Party, UML):-
Honourable Chairperson, the statement made by the Prime Minister in response to the questions of the members of parliament regarding the Nepal-India border dispute cannot be taken as a normal statement. I consider this statement to be anti-national, irresponsible, and contrary to diplomatic decorum and national interest. Our CPN UML party has also expressed serious objection to this matter and issued a statement yesterday. I also wish to inform this House that we have clearly stated our position.
Furthermore, the way the Prime Minister made such a self-destructive or anti-national statement here is a heinous attack on the dignity of three crore Nepali people and the sacrifices of our ancestors. I believe that this Prime Minister must be the first in world history to have made such a statement. The Prime Minister, in his capacity as the executive head, has made a statement that is self-destructive to his own country, without facts or evidence. Nepal has no history of encroaching on even an inch of land of any neighboring country.
Honourable Chairperson, for the executive head to speak factually on a sensitive issue like the border from the parliament's rostrum is a diplomatic crime that will destroy Nepal's long-standing just stance in international forums. It has worked to undermine our diplomatic decorum. Honourable Chairperson, the Prime Minister, who sits on the chair after taking an oath to protect the constitution and territorial integrity, has branded his own country as an aggressor. This is a deep betrayal of the nation. I wish to inform this House that such a statement will greatly weaken our claims over areas like Kalapani, Lipulek, and Limpiyadhura.
Honourable Chairperson, I wish to draw the attention of this House to another matter. I want to turn your attention towards the neighboring country Thailand. On August 29, 2025, the constitutional court there removed Prime Minister Petongtan Shinawatra from office immediately for breaching decorum and exhibiting unethical conduct in a private conversation. If a mere conversation can cost a Prime Minister their seat, then what right does any morality give the Prime Minister who claims their own territory as foreign while standing in a sovereign parliament to hold the Prime Minister's chair? Honourable Chairperson, therefore, giving such an irresponsible statement on the issue of national security shows the height of the Prime Minister's diplomatic immaturity. Trying to involve a friendly country like Britain in a dispute and trying to prove one's own country guilty undermines Nepal's policy of non-alignment and the principle of peaceful coexistence. What would the Nepali people who are ready to sacrifice their lives when the nation's borders are encroached upon think? What would the people living on the border of Nepal and India, guarding their borders, feel after hearing the Prime Minister's statement? I wish to draw the attention of this House to what is happening in their minds.
Furthermore, when sacrificing their lives for the nation's borders, and with such a statement from the Prime Minister in a sovereign parliament, the feelings of all three crore Nepali people have been hurt, I wish to request through this parliament. And further, while saying this, there can be no greater irony and insult than the Prime Minister himself saying, 'We have also encroached.' We strongly condemn this.
Honourable Chairperson, this anti-national and submissive thinking is absolutely unacceptable. The Prime Minister must immediately apologize to the Nepali people by coming to the parliament. He must immediately withdraw his statement and accept his moral downfall.

As I wish to state that to protect the dignity of such a respected position and maintain its high regard, a resignation should be submitted immediately and it should be accepted. Similarly, Articles 5 and 51 of the Constitution clearly state that it is the height of moral degradation for the country's chief protector to make statements against national interest. Therefore, until the Right Honourable Prime Minister comes to the House and retracts the statement he made on this matter, our party will not allow this parliament, this House, to proceed. I wish to state my position. Thank you.
Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Mahanta Thakur.
(13:35 hrs)
Honourable Mr. Mahanta Thakur (Loktantrik Samajwadi Party, Nepal):
(13:35 hrs)
I have occupied 13 bighas of land in India, I have not encroached upon it. Thank you.
Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Tul Prasad Bishwakarma.
(13:35 hrs)
Honourable Mr. Tul Prasad Bishwakarma (Rashtriya Janamorcha): Honourable
(13:36 hrs)
Chairperson, the statement made by our country's Prime Minister Mr. Balendra Shah in the House of Representatives on the 17th is extremely regrettable, objectionable, and anti-national, as I stated yesterday. What he said as the chief executive of the nation, did he say it from his own conscience, or did he say it after consulting with advisors or experts? I want to draw the attention of this House and the Nepali people to this matter. Our party has already issued a statement and protested his statement. Today, even India, which has not claimed it, has been told by him that we have also encroached upon it. What does it actually mean to encroach upon land, to encroach upon borders? And what does it mean to occupy? We need to differentiate these. On some borders, where rivers form the boundary, when the river changes its course, land on this side may fall on the other side, and sometimes land on the other side comes to this side. Naturally, people on the other side also occupy and cultivate land in Nepal, and Nepali people also cultivate land in the areas left by the river. This is not actually encroachment. This is occupation of land that has naturally shifted. However, actual border encroachment would mean the presence of the Nepali army there, or the presence of Nepali administration, and forceful occupation. That is not the situation. As in the case of Limpiyadhura, Kalapani, and Lipulek, the Indian army itself has established its barracks there for years and is claiming it. Actually, that is border encroachment. Therefore, we need to consider this matter. However, our Right Honourable Prime Minister, unable to differentiate these things, said that Nepal has encroached upon land in many places. Not only that, he also said that he was not aware of this. He said he only found out after becoming Prime Minister recently. And who informed him? We need to find that out. Who is that great person who provides information that is without proof, without facts, and is anti-national, against national interest, and against nationality? The people, the Nepali people, need to find that out.
Therefore, respected Honourable Chairperson, this border dispute over Nepal's land is not new. It has a long history. From Jhapa to Kanchanpur district, wherever Nepal's border adjoins India's border, India has encroached upon 72 places. This has been written in his book by Nepali border expert Buddhimaya Sherpa. After that, a joint mechanism between the Government of Nepal and the Government of India on border disputes was formed, which resolved issues in many places through dialogue. However, the Indian government was not ready to finalize it. The report was also submitted, but the Indian government did not accept it and has not accepted it to date. In this situation, where India is resorting to various tactics against Nepal, the unfortunate statement from the Prime Minister himself is undoubtedly a great tragedy for the Nepali people and the Nepali nation. Therefore, I would like to request here that until the Prime Minister comes to the rostrum, admits his mistake, and corrects his anti-national statements, we should not allow this House to proceed. I wish to conclude my statement by saying that today's session should also not proceed. Thank you.
Honourable Chairperson: Honourable members are speaking. And
(13:49 hrs)
Honourable members have expressed their views, haven't they? Now, I have been seriously alerted. Honourable ministers are present here, representing the government. They have also been alerted, and as per the demand, this matter will certainly be conveyed to the Government of Nepal or the Right Honourable Prime Minister. Therefore, I believe it would be wise for the National Assembly to continue its proceedings while seriously presenting their issues. Considering our past tradition and the current situation, I earnestly request the Honourable members to cooperate in advancing our proceedings by remaining in their seats. Honourable members, please remain in your seats.
Honourable members, there is one item on today's agenda: the "Alternative Development Finance Bill". Now, it will be difficult for all of you. If this bill cannot be presented in the House today, it will slip from our hands. Its deadline is the 22nd. If it is presented in the House today, there will be a 24-hour period for suggestions. Amendments will not be made, only suggestions. Tomorrow it will be the 24th, and the day after tomorrow it can be passed. Our session will not run for a few days from the 21st onwards. I believe seven, eight, or nine sessions will not run, only 3-4 days. Seven Presidiums, the House of Representatives and the National Assembly. After that, what will happen is that the Alternative Finance Bill will slip from the hands of the National Assembly, and the message it gives to the Nepali people, what we have earned so far in the National Assembly, I fear it might be tarnished. Therefore, if we at least present that bill today and leave, tomorrow will be a new day, and we can think in a new way. Therefore, my humble request to the Honourable members is to remain in your seats and cooperate in advancing some proceedings.
Did you not hear what I said? After the chairperson asks everyone to sit down, the proceedings will move forward. Therefore, I once again say, it is a dilemma here. I think this is happening for the first time in the history of this House, perhaps in the National Assembly. The National Assembly has a record of doing such things. 100% opposition from Honourable members. It is probably rare in the world for a House to say "let's not run the session" by standing up. 100% opposition, and then running it. So far, whatever we have done, I think we have done almost everything with 100% support. But here, the opposition is also 100%. Therefore, the message that the opposition is 100% has gone. This matter has reached the Prime Minister. It has reached the Government of Nepal. It has reached the entire political sphere. So, this is the message we need to give. I said it yesterday too, but it's not necessary to say it now because what the Prime Minister said was not in our House, but in the House of Representatives. I urge you to go there and do whatever you want, and let us move forward. Yes, that's the point. We heard that he said it, but he didn't speak here. Therefore, the opposition that arose there in support of his statement. We supported that opposition yesterday and today until this time, which is fine. Now, I urge you to move forward with our proceedings. I request the Honourable members again from the Secretariat, it's about to be presented.
Honourable members, the next meeting of the National Assembly will be held on Wednesday, Jestha 20, 2083 BS at 12:15 PM, and this meeting is adjourned until then.
(Thereafter, the next meeting was adjourned until Wednesday, Jestha 20, 2083 BS at 12:15 PM.)
Adjourned: 13:49 hrs.

sections.summary_en: Honourable Member Padam Bahadur Pariyar raised concerns about the Prime Minister's statement regarding border encroachment, calling it irresponsible and against national interest. He demanded clarification and an apology. Honourable Member Ghanashyam Rizal echoed these sentiments, expressing disagreement and concern over the Prime Minister's statement and urging him to apologize. Honourable Member Roshni Mechhe strongly condemned the Prime Minister's statement as anti-national and a betrayal of the country, demanding an apology and withdrawal of the statement.
